title: Reed-Solomon error correction
summary: Reed-Solomon (RS) codes are block-based error-correcting codes. RS(n,k): n total symbols, k data symbols, n-k parity symbols. Can correct up to t = (n-k)/2 errors (or n-k erasures). Used in QR codes, CDs/DVDs, RAID, deep space communication, and digital TV.

ext.summary: Reed-Solomon (RS) codes are block-based error-correcting codes. RS(n,k): n total symbols, k data symbols, n-k parity symbols. Can correct up to t = (n-k)/2 errors (or n-k erasures). Used in QR codes, CDs/DVDs, RAID, deep space communication, and digital TV.

structure.meaning: n = total codeword length, k = data length, n-k = parity length. Usually n = 2^m - 1 (e.g., 255 for 8-bit symbols).
Can correct up to t symbol errors. Or n-k erasures (known positions).
Multiply data polynomial by generator polynomial. Or use systematic form: data + parity.
Berlekamp-Massey algorithm for error locator polynomial. Chien search for error positions. Forney algorithm for error values.
255 total, 223 data, 32 parity. Corrects 16 errors. Used in many systems.
255 total, 239 data, 16 parity. Corrects 8 errors. Used in QR codes.

notes: Reed-Solomon codes are maximum distance separable (MDS): d_min = n-k+1 (optimal).
RS codes are used in QR codes (correct up to 30% damage), CDs (CIRC), DVDs, Blu-ray, RAID-6, and deep space (Voyager, Mars rovers).
RS codes work over Galois fields (GF(2^m)). Common: GF(2^8) for byte-level codes.
Concatenated codes (RS + convolutional) are used in deep space communication.
Reed-Solomon is the basis of most modern error correction.
